wstep: This card follows the citric-acid mozzarella recipe of the UCCE Master Food Preservers of Amador/Calaveras County, adapted from University of Alaska Fairbanks Extension FNH-00063. [T:MLE-087]

ostrzezenia.tekst: Make this cheese only from pasteurized milk; raw milk must be pasteurized before it is used for cheese. [T:MLE-015]
Do not pasteurize raw milk in a microwave oven, because it does not heat the milk evenly. [T:MLE-013]

akapity: The recipe does not give a total making time, so this card does not promise a quick cheese; do not shorten any step to save time. [T:-]
UCCE uses 1 gallon of milk that is not ultra-pasteurized, because ultra-pasteurized milk does not separate into curds and whey. [T:MLE-087]
Dissolve 1 1/2 teaspoons of citric acid in 1 cup of cool, chlorine-free water. [T:MLE-087]
Dissolve 1/4 rennet tablet or 1/4 teaspoon of liquid rennet in 1/4 cup of cool, chlorine-free water. [T:MLE-087]
You can add 1 teaspoon of cheese salt, or leave it out. [T:MLE-087]
Pour the citric acid solution into the pot, add the milk and stir gently. [T:MLE-087]
Heat the milk slowly to 90 °F (about 32 °C) while stirring. [T:MLE-087]
Take the pot off the heat and fold in the rennet solution, top to bottom, for about 30 seconds. [T:MLE-087]
Cover the pot and leave it undisturbed for 5 minutes. [T:MLE-087]
Cut the curd in a 1-inch (2.5 cm) checkerboard pattern. [T:MLE-087]
Put the pot back on the heat and warm the curd to 105 °F (about 41 °C), stirring slowly and gently. [T:MLE-088]
Take it off the heat and keep stirring slowly for 2–5 minutes. [T:MLE-088]
Move the curd with a slotted spoon to a colander over a bowl and add 3/4–1 teaspoon of salt. [T:MLE-088]
Heat two-thirds of the whey to 175 °F (about 79 °C). [T:MLE-088]
The whey is very hot, so dip the curd into it with the slotted spoon or heat-resistant gloves. [T:MLE-088]
Keep the whey at 170–175 °F (about 77–79 °C), and work, fold and stretch the curd until it is smooth and shiny. [T:MLE-088]
Shape the cheese into balls and cool them in ice water. [T:MLE-088]
Keep the cheese in an airtight container or wrapped in plastic wrap in the refrigerator and eat it within a week, or freeze it for up to a month. [T:MLE-057]
Pregnant women should avoid cheeses made from unpasteurized milk. [T:MLE-049]
